b: God tells Hosea to marry a woman who will be unfaithful, so that his own life becomes the message. Israel's idolatry is presented as adultery, and God's response as the grief of a betrayed husband who will not let go.

1.t: The prophet's life becomes the message. The children are given names that are sentences of judgement.

11.h: How can I give you up
11.t: God's internal conflict expressed as a parent's. My heart recoils within me, my compassion grows warm. Matthew quotes verse 1 of Jesus.

11.h: Out of Egypt I called my son
11.t: Quoted by Matthew of Jesus, reading Israel's history as fulfilled in him.

3.t: Hosea pays to redeem his own wife. The price is roughly that of a slave.

6.t: Quoted twice by Jesus in Matthew, both times to people who were technically correct and missing the point.

14.t: The book ends with an invitation and a promise to heal their waywardness and love them freely.

2.h: I will lead her into the wilderness
2.t: And speak tenderly to her. Judgement and wooing in the same sentence.

4.t: The charge is against priests who rejected knowledge, not against ignorant people.

5.h: Then I will return to my lair
5.t: Until they admit their guilt. God described as withdrawing deliberately.

7.h: A flat loaf not turned over
7.t: Burnt on one side and raw on the other. Hosea's image for half-hearted religion.

10.t: It is time to seek the LORD until he comes and showers righteousness on you.

12.t: Maintain love and justice, and wait for your God always.

13.h: Where, O death, is your victory
13.t: Paul takes this line into 1 Corinthians 15.

8.t: And reap the whirlwind. Consequences larger than the cause.

9.h: The prophet is considered a fool
9.t: Israel dismisses God's messengers as mad.
